# noisebench

> In the latest run (finished 29 July 2026; 20 AI models, 100 Polymarket questions and 23,861 answers), the least noisy forecaster was gpt-5.6-sol-pro (OpenAI) with a noise score of 4.3%, and the noisiest was mistral-large-2512 (Mistral) at 16.2%. The average across all models was 8.6%. Lower is better: 0% means a model gave the same answer every time it was asked, in every wording.

noisebench is an open benchmark of judgment noise in large language models used as forecasters. Each model is asked the same live Polymarket questions repeatedly, in both the Yes and the No wording, and is asked which of two markets is likelier in all four negation combinations of the pair. Made by Luis Fominaya Parra (https://luisfominaya.com/). MIT licensed.

## Pages

- [Overview](https://noisebench.com/): the Noise Index, its five parts, and noise against cost.
- [Compare](https://noisebench.com/compare): two models side by side.
- [Markets](https://noisebench.com/markets): every question, the panel's odds against the market price.
- [Details](https://noisebench.com/details): methodology and the five measures.

## Data

- [metrics.json](https://noisebench.com/data/metrics.json): per-model and per-question metrics.
- [negation.json](https://noisebench.com/data/negation.json): negation breakdown.
- [noise.json](https://noisebench.com/data/noise.json): noise scales and subsets.
- [run.json](https://noisebench.com/data/run.json): run configuration.
